narrative: OMX30 faces headwinds from a sharp Treasury yield rally (US 10Y +72bp to 5.293%, worst level since 2002) that pressures both growth valuations and real estate refinancing costs. European equity markets showed broad weakness yesterday (DAX -0.19%, CAC -0.77%, FTSE -1.06%), while Asia's strength (Nikkei +3.30%) failed to provide meaningful support—net correlation signal is -0.136%, a subtle bearish tilt. Technically, the index sits 4.2% above its 200-MA (still in bull structure) but is hamstrung by weak momentum: ADX at 4.3 with bearish directional bias, MACD below signal line (histogram -2.825), and RSI neutral at 49.55. The index resides in the lower half of its Bollinger envelope and is 2.5% off its 52-week high. Oil's sharp 2.91% decline and modest strength in gold (+0.53%) create mixed sector signals. Key risk: further Treasury weakness could trigger a capitulation selloff, while strength in USD/SEK (+0.31%) provides an export tailwind to offset yields.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens under pressure on the back of a historic Treasury bond sell-off (10Y at 5.293%, +72bp overnight). European peers finished weak across the board yesterday; expect cautious sentiment into the Stockholm open. The technical picture is muddled: we remain in a bull structure (4.2% above 200-MA) but momentum is fading—ADX extremely weak at 4.3, MACD rolling over, and RSI neutral. Watch the 3123 level (yesterday's close) and the 50-MA at ~3130 for intraday support; 3085 (lower Bollinger) is the hard floor. Banks may see initial support from wider NIM prospects, but real estate and tech will struggle with yield pressure. The USD/SEK strength (+0.31%) is a green flag for exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson), but energy weakness (Brent -2.91%) is a headwind to industrials. Expect range-bound trading with a slight downward lean until US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET provide fresh direction.
